title: An Empirical Argument for Presentism
version: Author preprint 'Forthcoming in Oxford Studies in Metaphysics', 23 pages, Sanders Foundation upload 2022-09 (same version Lettie cites as PhilArchive v1, 2022-09-26). Published: OSM 14 (2025) pp. 63-88, doi:10.1093/9780198952763.003.0003; published text not compared.
locators: p.3 Markovian Chance; pp.3-4 relativistic reformulation over Cauchy foliations
pp.4-6 intrinsic velocity, Near Markovian, Markovian*
pp.6-10 section 3 eternalism; p.7 fn10 0011/000111 toy worlds; pp.9-10 locality dilemma
pp.10-15 section 4; p.14 Nomic Presentism and schema; p.15 chance
p.16 (*) and fn18 growing block, fn20 falsifiability; p.17 fn24 local presentisms
assumptions: Markovian* is an empirical feature of best theories; the intrinsic state at a time is well defined; non-Humean causal powers (4.1) or Nomic Presentism (4.2); Bayesian confirmation with rational priors.
conclusion: Authors' claim: certain non-Humean presentisms entail Markovianism; eternalist views give no reason to expect it; hence substantial confirmation of NHP.
proof_status: Philosophical argument read in full; the p.14 schema is valid as stated. Our RESULT.md argues the certain proposition is the presentist reformulation, not the property of the laws.
open_questions: Does the published OSM 14 text differ from the 2022 preprint?
Which semantics for Nomic Presentism do the authors intend?
relevance: Rival argument: Markovian laws as empirical evidence for presentism; directly about what the past fixes beyond the present.
limits: Preprint version only; citing literature beyond three replies unread.

title: Explaining Markovian time
version: PhilArchive preprint dated September 2024, 'Forthcoming in Analysis'; published Analysis online 2024-12-04, doi:10.1093/analys/anae070 (published text not compared).
assumptions: B&I's Markovianism granted; probability over possible worlds can be meaningfully posed.
conclusion: Author's claim: Markovianism is one of many individually improbable but collectively probable Markovian-like properties; (*) holds but rational priors can leave NHP improbable.
proof_status: Read in full; Bayesian example arithmetic checked (0.001/0.01099 ~ 0.091).
relevance: Main published reply; does not examine what the section 4.2 derivation makes certain.

title: Temporal Ontology and Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
version: Philosophies 11(2):45, published 2026-03-22 (open access HTML via Exa fetch).
locators: sections 1, 2.1-2.2, 4, 5 read; section 3 headings only; 5.3 growing block
assumptions: Accepts B&I's explanatory premise for the mirror argument; non-Markovian foundations treated as speculative.
conclusion: Author's claim: if non-Markovianity is fundamental, eternalism prima facie explains it better; growing block faces a time-symmetry problem.
relevance: Converse pressure; no Bell or relativity treatment.
limits: Section 3 physics survey not read in detail.

title: Temporal Membranes: Non-Markovian Dependence and Selective Temporal Inheritance
version: Philosophies 11(6):201, published 2026-10-30 (open access HTML via Exa fetch, truncated).
locators: sections 1-4 and 5.1-5.2 read; 5.2 onward truncated in fetch
assumptions: Process-relational schema; distinctions among senses of Markovianity.
conclusion: Author's claim: Markovianity and non-Markovianity underdetermine temporal ontology; selective temporal inheritance is the neglected burden.
relevance: Supplies the general Markovian-embedding point applied in RESULT.md O3.

title: Locality, Probability and the Relevance of History
locators: Definitions 1-3; Principles 1-4; Propositions 1-3 statements; section on irrelevance of history (Principle 4 with translation clause); footnotes 10, 17, 18
assumptions: World-theories (M,E,W) with surfaces; probabilistic world-theories; Principle 4 includes a time-translation map.
conclusion: Author's claim: Probabilistic Locality and Irrelevance of History jointly imply Local Causality, so Bell violations show history is relevant.
open_questions: Does Proposition 3 survive dropping the translation clause?
relevance: Local event-wise Markov-chance condition that Bell violations pressure; footnote 10 states the backward-determinism point (O2).
limits: Partial read; does not cite B&I; the transfer to B&I is our conjecture.

title: State maps for linear systems
relevance: Nearest formal prior for O1 and O3: 'Markovian' behaviour as closure under concatenation at equal values, and the axiom of state; the Willems 2002 lecture notes describe past-induced (Nerode) state construction.
limits: Only the section 3 definitions seen in a search excerpt; journal details not verified here; linear time-invariant setting.
